newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Steel & Tube expects to match 95/96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Steel & Tube expects to match 95/96 profit.

text.p: Engineering and contracting firm Steel and Tube said on Tuesday it expected its profit for the 11 months to May 31 to approximate on a pro rata basis the previous year's NZ$25.3 million net profit.
Earlier, the company reported an unaudited profit after tax of NZ$10.96 million for the five months to November 30, against $11.38 million for the corresponding period last year.
It also declared a dividend of 20 cents per share.

The directors said sales rose to NZ$188 million from $133 million, due primarily to the inclusion of a full five months' revenue from acquired companies AJ Forsyth & Co and Southern Cross Engineering Holdings.
The company said the domestic steel operations of distribution, processing and reinforcing performed strongly over the period, although a changed product mix saw a slight reduction in profitability.
Despite a NZ$26 million increase in sales, the profit of the engineering and fabrication operations was well below expectations.
Steel and Tube said this was due to problems on major contracts and difficult conditions in the forestry sector.
The company is half owned by Tubemakers of Australia Ltd in which the Broken Hill Pty Ltd has a controlling interest.
